As the new school year begins, a growing number of Americans support an outright ban on students using mobile phones in classrooms.

The new school year is already underway, and calls for banning iPhones on campuses continue to grow.

That's right—although it's still July, summer seems to have ended early. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive year that the first day of school no longer falls in August.

Apple is ushering in the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 will receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in participating states can also enjoy a limited-time sales tax waiver.

Although the back-to-school deals are exciting, the use of mobile phones during class is increasingly attracting backlash.

Featured comment posted by GreenPizza

I've never seen any data supporting the claim that "allowing students to use mobile phones during school shooting incidents can reduce risk." In fact, reducing distractions in the classroom is what truly allows us to achieve our learning goals.

A latest survey by Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using mobile phones during class, up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% now oppose such bans on campus.

Support for a stricter "all-day ban"—prohibiting students from using mobile phones on campus throughout the entire day—has grown even more significantly. For the first time, Americans supporting an all-day ban outnumber those who oppose it.

The report also noted that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about classroom bans and all-day bans, but since 2024, support rates have risen across all age groups. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools mandate that students can only use iPhones inside the classroom, implement an all-day ban, or leave it up to students and parents to decide? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
